criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission, need with bleaching statistics, and single-spacecraft rationale given. Users only vague: Australian facilities and marine scientists mentioned, no clear operator vs customers distinction, lacking detail and specific references.

evidence.quote: fluid lensing has been used in combination with AI analysis
is operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All sub-topics covered with STK screenshots, access table and plots. Significant technical errors: 87.79 deg not SSO at 600km, Kourou latitude 45.05N, RAAN logic flawed, future vehicle speculative. Design inconsistent but adequate.

evidence.quote: will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle
an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 87.7924°

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Summarises orbit, launch, ground station and benefit, notes Vega E risk. Generic, short, repeats proposal without detailed evidence-based findings or quantified performance conclusions.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and executive summary, readable. Figures/tables inconsistently captioned, formatting uneven. References bare URLs, includes Wikipedia explicitly prohibited, citation style poor.

technical_issues.issue: Inclination 87.79 deg for 600km SSO is wrong; should be ~97.8 deg as own Image 3 shows ~97.8 deg at 600km.
Kourou latitude stated as 45.05 deg N, actual ~5.2 deg N; invalidates two-windows-per-day claim.
RAAN 27.33 deg tied to launch facility location misunderstands RAAN/LSTAN for SSO.
Uses Wikipedia Timeline of spaceflight despite task banning Wikipedia.

overall: Single-satellite reef monitor concept with plausible SSO and ground-station analysis, but marred by critical orbit-mechanics errors and weak referencing.

feedback.summary: You proposed a clear single-satellite reef-monitoring concept with STK-supported SSO and ground-station analysis. Your strength is covering all required topics, but critical orbit-mechanics errors and vague users and referencing keep you at Adequate. Fixing those will lift you toward Accomplished.
next_steps: Correct your 600 km SSO to ~97.8 deg as your Image 3 shows and fix Kourou latitude to ~5.2 deg N and RAAN/LSTAN logic with textbook references.
Clarify in your Introduction who operates you spacecraft versus who are customers, adding specific Australian agencies and literature on bleaching and fluid lensing.
Upgrade presentation: caption all figures/tables consistently, replace bare URLs and prohibited Wikipedia with proper cited sources.

criteria.C1: You did well in your Introduction stating your fluid lensing mission, bleaching need, and that only one satellite is required. For Accomplished, distinguish your operator versus customers beyond Australian facilities and add detailed, referenced descriptions.
criteria.C2: You covered launch with Vega E, 600 km orbit, maneuvers and ground control with STK screenshots and Image 4. For Accomplished, you must correct your 87.7924 deg to ~97.8 deg, Kourou 45.05 deg N error, and RAAN logic with accurate evidence.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion usefully summarises your Vega E selection, orbit, ground station and Vega E risk. For Accomplished, move beyond repeating your proposal to detailed conclusions drawn from your evidence with quantified performance.
criteria.C4: You used clear headings and an executive summary with readable writing. For Accomplished, consistently caption figures/tables like your DN path plots, fix formatting, and use proper in-text citations without Wikipedia URLs.
